Hear directly from NDTC Founder and CEO Kelly Dietrich and special guest A’shanti F. Gholar, President of Emerge, on [Thursday, January 20 at 1pm ET](https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..9ZujIwCB5zKiSoGTsTs0Vjs4t1DWG2XVaYezCE0F0fI) on how you can begin to recruit potential candidates in your community.

Building blue is about people first and foremost.

And some of the most important people are the candidates that end up running for office!

This is not a cut and dry task; recruitment requires tact and skill.

A’shanti and Kelly will share the best practices of effective recruitment, as well as answering any questions about the process and how it looks in real life.

Come with all your best questions and we can kick off our first Q&A of 2022 with a bang.

[There’s a limited number of attendees, so RSVP while you can!](https://t.dripemail2.com/c/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..9ZujIwCB5zKiSoGTsTs0Vjs4t1DWG2XVaYezCE0F0fI)

But this fight is far from over. This fight to protect you will not be easy. We’ve got all the Republicans in the House on it and now the Supreme Court, do I have your support as well? God Bless Freedom, Fred Keller (Taking the values of PA's 12th District to Congress) Paid for by Fred Keller for Congress Our mailing address is: Fred Keller for Congeress, PO Box 61893 Harrisburg, PA 17106 Don't want to receive our emails anymore?

| | Dear Friend,

I felt compelled this week to write an open letter to one of my opponents, Stan Pulliam, about his shortsighted proposal for Oregon’s homelessness crisis. The crisis cannot be solved by stigmatizing and criminalizing all unsheltered people. This crisis needs a leader with proactive solutions to get the unsheltered off our streets and into rehabilitation. It will not be solved by politicians with soundbites.
Here is my letter below:
---
|
---
| Stan,

With this letter, I’m hoping to give you a better understanding of the unsheltered population in Oregon and what must be done to address the crisis we are now facing because of previous inaction and very poor leadership.

You state the crisis needs an adult in the room (a rather poor choice of words), but who better to be that person than me – a now successful adult who for nearly a year lived a homeless life?

I am shocked to read your posts, eblasts, and writings stating that those “camping” in cars and tents are choosing to live that way because they are bad characters with evil intentions. Stan, at age 15, my family broke apart and I was homeless in Southern Oregon. I slept in cars, couch surfed, and spent a lot of time in parks. I and the homeless community I lived among had no evil intentions. We were down on our luck. We had a singular goal – to survive without a home.

Homelessness is destroying our once beautiful cities and is economically distressing our business climate. Allowing people to live in squalor and danger is not compassionate. But false accusations, misrepresentations, and oversimplifications of a multi-tiered problem and knee jerk solutions are not leadership.

You falsely suggest that people camping in public right of ways and on sidewalks are “not people who have found themselves in a tough spot. They are mostly criminals.” You are so wrong, and this oversimplification of Oregon’s systemic homelessness problem has caused you to suggest impractical short-term solutions without any positive long-term effects.

Not all people struggling with chronic homelessness have the same challenges, and a comprehensive approach to getting the unsheltered off our streets with objectives, accountability, and deliverables is way past due. But you must not let anger, frustration, and campaign soundbites cloud your perspective.

Most people do not initially choose to live unsheltered in freezing temperatures, in soaked bedding on hard pavements, and in danger. The unsheltered are not “mostly criminals,” as you suggest. I was one of the lucky homeless individuals. My bilingual grandmother rescued me from the streets and rehabilitated me with tough love and strong guidance.

Oregon’s next CEO must get the unsheltered off our streets by putting a multi-tiered support system in place and levels of care to rehabilitate. But first, let us agree that merely throwing money at the crisis and oversimplifying the problem without objectives, coordination, accountability, and deliverables will result in dismal outcomes.

[Here is a link to my Comprehensive Approach to Addressing Homelessness.](https://jessicagomezforgovernor.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=38928f39f4567607835360484&id=6a56124592&e=7e91be8cad)

Sincerely yours,
Jessica Gomez
---
|
---
| Friends, we simply cannot waste this opportunity to restore balance to our state by embracing those who don't have real solutions to our problems. If you agree, will you chip in $10, $25, or $50 to our values-centered campaign to show our opponents that policy-based solutions are the only way to move forward?

Today, we got two very big decisions from the U.S. Supreme Court. I wanted to be sure that you heard from me directly on what it all means. Friend, Today, we got two very big decisions from the U.S. Supreme Court. I wanted to be sure that you heard from me directly on what it all means. First, the good news: **The Supreme Court has agreed with us and halted the Biden administration’s vaccine mandate that would have applied to an estimated 84 million private employees in America. ** The ruling gives welcome relief to thousands of employers and employees throughout our state who now will not lose their jobs because of their healthcare decisions. I have said from the very beginning that federal mandates are NOT the answer and that they are NOT constitutional. The appropriate way for the government to respond to COVID is to provide Kansans with the best available information and trust Kansans to make the right decisions with that information. [](http://links.schmidtforkansas.com/u/click?_t=4eb8bd5dcca54a0b993a2eb1eb42ba73&_m=c7f06253136144c4a46407ba3d7f9884&_e=yfs2u8NGom3Kb4wK3F9epm92FZjbmB3FZbHaX0kGgh-EkNbim0ukYVPX7iWoBqV5tqDUN9ZPz15-ti86Pr342DKCsbd5M0zoZjYcJ2cqqWBEQy2xSgJnXVCRdGHuDGaPBY9gJb1BxB_rbxCXfpIHl8gDA6d8Ye981xla42a_q-f3kHiYUc1mer97CLU2b1UwteD4MQmxTmtrk68ABBS39fQDAnaOtfuBVa3i8HyDfkWOQD3AY4A1b2o33ksOruS_wksyYs940KUX-zlUTwJtSJimnBIe0Jn6XgY_sli_7NOCMJ7jLcAqyYG-mLWnuLrYW5jqLPy_gApWq2sR45j3mX7TqNgP7X3hJG8qkuidRft352ovBqZgLC71cILMwWD9OpWkPhvt7pzBaZIwFTtBbTy9M0nQIUQJi9jm75Jst4DACI41hUrhTwHI1Gd4U-BEsBDB1G4pIWpbeVf_mdpz_pBBBeem_Eh-NlP3VAJo7LI%3D) Unfortunately, today’s rulings are a mixed bag for Kansas. While the Court blocked the mandate for private employees, in a separate ruling it allowed - for now - the vaccine mandate for healthcare workers to be implemented while the case heads back to lower courts for further arguments. This disappointing decision to uphold the so-called “CMS mandate” is likely to aggravate the shortage of nurses and other healthcare professionals that already is causing serious disruption to the delivery of care throughout our state. We’ll keep up the fight, and thanks to Republicans in the Legislature taking decisive action during the special session, healthcare workers in Kansas have robust religious liberty and medical exemption protections. But there is no doubt - the Biden administration’s one-size-fits-all approach is causing substantial harm in the lives, liberties and livelihoods of many Kansans. As attorney general, I promise to never stop fighting for your individual liberty in the courts. As governor, I promise to trust you with your healthcare decisions. I won’t make you choose between a job and a jab. But I’m going to need a lot of help to win this race. ### **Still no Legislative Inspector General **
We do not need any more evidence of the culture of corruption in Springfield but consider that the Legislative Inspector General position remains vacant.
Carol Pope announced last summer that she would be leaving her post at the end of December. She cited the lack of seriousness for ethics in the Illinois General Assembly as the main reason for her departure.
To further prove the General Assembly’s lack of seriousness for ethics, the Legislative Inspector General position remains vacant despite the fact the Legislature has known of the vacancy for months.
This is how far gone our state’s leadership is when it comes to anti-corruption initiatives. They refuse to give the Legislative Inspector General any real power to combat ethics violations and even refuse to take the absolute minimum step of filling what is largely a symbolic position. They are not interested in ethics reform enough to even make a symbolic gesture.
We need new leadership in Springfield, and we need it now.
### Why won’t Pritzker stand up for Chicago Public School students?
During the recent teacher walkout in Chicago, which has effectively shutting down classes in the nation’s third largest city, Governor JB Pritzker has remained strangely silent.
Chicago Mayor Lori Lightfoot is standing up to the powerful teachers’ unions and trying to get in person learning restored, but where is Gov. Pritzker?
Pritzker is afraid of the consequences of taking on the teachers’ unions and so he remains silent. For the sake of our kids, for the sake of the mental and emotional health of our kids, he has got to step up as a leader.
Of course, we know he won’t, which is one of many reasons why he must be defeated in November.
### Illinois is officially the abortion capital of the Midwest
As thousands gathered for the March for Life in Chicago, abortion advocates in Illinois are continuing to make our state a leader for abortion services.
According to Jennifer Welch, president and CEO of Planned Parenthood of Illinois, every state bordering Illinois has laws in place to end abortion should the United States Supreme Court overturn Roe v. Wade.
“Tens of thousands of people will be in this big abortion desert,” Welch said. “Illinois already serves as a haven in the Midwest for abortion care, and that’s just going to multiply.”
In 2019, there were 7,534 non-residents who received an abortion in Illinois up from 5,668 in 2018\.
Wouldn’t it be nice if Governor Pritzker and the far-left leaders in the House and the Senate prioritized helping working families instead of promoting policies to destroy them? No wonder people are leaving our state in droves.

body:

| | | |
---
---
---
| [](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001H81VKo4ImuIX42hazisG97oH9AcHyRko0_DVeVO5Fdc4qrMso4DCsbi3-TBEXessqGT4tQtvqMMv-fwDhOTadGlxRLVbxe8COX0ZVzko8RkFp-8-IjPc_E0EUP5dq2k7Dx3mxfhuRVN5FnxeBOLxIw==&c=w9AyHbLl_F4dePSC6kR45B8LgA_rvXshYCGPzKsucMRlqxesxtYS_A==&ch=uODVxOrBnogZHt1i7UlNrWGdmtd24w4fu6MugUtw_zNoC6hmtqSkWQ==)
---
|
---
Dear Friend,
This past Sunday, our nation recognized National Law Enforcement Appreciation Day. It's always important for us to honor the selfless work first responders do every day to keep us safe, and to thank them for their dedication.
Unfortunately, first responders aren't getting the help and support they need. In particular, alongside calls to defund the police, police officers, firefighters, and EMT's across our state are under threat of losing their jobs due to vaccine mandates. This is currently an issue specifically in Boston, where a vaccine mandate is due to take effect later this week.
I am proud to stand with Boston First Responders United and others as they fight against vaccine mandates. I am not opposed to vaccines, but I strongly oppose vaccine mandates as a condition of employment.
Public servants across our state are losing their jobs because they're unwilling to submit to medical treatment they don't want, and that's just wrong. It disrespects peoples' liberty, it's an abuse of power by the government, and it should not be happening.
I'm proud to always #BackTheBlue. I hope you'll join me in supporting our law enforcement officers and all other first responders. They have our back every day; let's pledge to have their back when they need us, too.
Thanks, as always, for your support.
Sincerely,
---
---
Geoff Diehl Republican Candidate for Governor
---
---
---
---
|
---
---
I'm working hard every day to be your next Governor. We need someone to stand up for individual rights and liberties, and I pledge to do that. But, in order to get there, I need your help.

clean_body: First responders have our back, it's important for us to support them too. | | | | | == | Dear Friend, This past Sunday, our nation recognized National Law Enforcement Appreciation Day. It's always important for us to honor the selfless work first responders do every day to keep us safe, and to thank them for their dedication. Unfortunately, first responders aren't getting the help and support they need. In particular, alongside calls to defund the police, police officers, firefighters, and EMT's across our state are under threat of losing their jobs due to vaccine mandates. This is currently an issue specifically in Boston, where a vaccine mandate is due to take effect later this week. I am proud to stand with Boston First Responders United and others as they fight against vaccine mandates. I am not opposed to vaccines, but I strongly oppose vaccine mandates as a condition of employment. Public servants across our state are losing their jobs because they're unwilling to submit to medical treatment they don't want, and that's just wrong. It disrespects peoples' liberty, it's an abuse of power by the government, and it should not be happening. I'm proud to always #BackTheBlue. I hope you'll join me in supporting our law enforcement officers and all other first responders. They have our back every day; let's pledge to have their back when they need us, too. Thanks, as always, for your support. Sincerely, Geoff Diehl Republican Candidate for Governor | I'm working hard every day to be your next Governor. name: Geoff Diehl
subject: Join Me and Run for Office!
body:
2022 is the Time to Stand Up
| | | |
---
---
---
| Friends,
There's a runaway train of progressive ideas in our state. It's leading us far in the wrong direction, causing the cost of goods to rise and parents to be shut out of their children's education. It's time for candidates who care about the future of our state to stand up and run for office.
If you run in 2022 as a Republican for State Representative, State Senate, and municipal offices like City Council, Selectman, and School Committee, you'll be joining forces with the Massachusetts Republican Party and the Diehl for Governor campaign to run as a TEAM.
Now is the time! In 2010, in the mid-point of President Obama's first term, Massachusetts Republicans picked up 19 seats in the state Legislature, and elected Scott Brown as our U.S. Senator. We can repeat this success, and increase those numbers, in 2022. But I can't do it alone; I need your help.
Please join me and run for office. Attend one of the MassGOP's upcoming training sessions for candidates, and learn more about how to run successfully for office:

| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE FRIDAY, JANUARY 14, 2022
BURT JONES RAISES $3.75 MILLION, ENDS YEAR WITH $3.4 MILLION CASH ON HAND
JACKSON, Ga. - Today, conservative, Trump-endorsed candidate for Lieutenant Governor of Georgia Burt Jones announced that his campaign will report raising $3.75 million during the fundraising period, ending the year with approximately $3.4 million cash on hand. This massive haul reflects the overwhelming support for Burt's campaign across the state and country, demonstrates his clear momentum in the race, and proves that he is the only candidate with the record, message and resources to deliver a strong victory for Georgia families in November.
"The outpouring of support for our campaign from every corner of the state has been truly incredible and humbling," said Burt Jones. "From President Trump's endorsement to support from grassroots leaders across the state, we hit the ground running from day one and never looked back. Our message of more jobs, lower taxes, better schools, safer communities, and secure elections is clearly resonating with voters who are ready for fresh leadership. I'm looking forward to continue traveling the state, meeting with voters, listening to their stories, and building momentum toward a big win in November to become Georgia's next Lieutenant Governor."

Hey there friend,

I know you get a lot of emails from my team and I, but the truth is, it’s never easy to ask for money. But I wouldn’t be doing it (and I wouldn’t be running for governor) if I didn’t believe with all my heart that we’re going to defeat Gov. DeSantis.

And my promise to you is that I’m doing everything within my power to make sure we beat him, which brings me to something really important: I recently checked in with my finance team, and they’re worried.

That means I’m worried too.

**[My finance staffers set a mid-month goal of $20,000, and they’re concerned because we still have $6,421 left to raise. So I need to ask: Will you donate $5, $8, or even $12 to help us meet this goal by tomorrow?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/40670291/325399166/567982044?refcode=20220114_f_1_ND&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTYxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZDU4YThjNC0zZTc1LWVjMTEtOTRmNi1jODk2NjUwZDQ0NDIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tw240M0lUnTXk3IWtG8kj6sakVexzecgrxXvFXrfHLg=)**

You know as well as I that **Florida can’t afford another four years of Gov. DeSantis’s failed leadership.** Even now, as the Omicron variant sweeps across our state, he _refuses_ to make COVID-19 testing accessible to keep our schools, businesses, and economy open.

We must defeat DeSantis, and we must do it this year.

Fortunately, our momentum is surging! My team and I have held more than 80 events to organize Floridians, DeSantis’s approval ratings have dropped, and polls have shown me either closing in on the governor – or beating him outright.

**[But we really can’t afford to fall behind, not now. So I’m hoping you can spare a few dollars and help my team catch up to our mid-month goal.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/40670292/325399167/567982044?refcode=20220114_f_1_ND&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTYxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZDU4YThjNC0zZTc1LWVjMTEtOTRmNi1jODk2NjUwZDQ0NDIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tw240M0lUnTXk3IWtG8kj6sakVexzecgrxXvFXrfHLg=)**

Thanks and God bless,
Charlie

| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Press@NickForNJ.com January 14, 2022 De Gregorio Raises $403,000 in Challenge to Gottheimer, Announces Endorsements of LD39 Assembly Members
FAIR LAWN - Today, Nick De Gregorio, a Marine Veteran and Republican Candidate for Congress in New Jersey's Fifth Congressional District, announced that his campaign will report over $403,000 raised on his year-end report for 2021 with $360,000 cash on hand.
"We are grateful to all of our enthusiastic supporters for meeting the great momentum we are feeling across the Fifth District with the resources we will need to take on the disastrous Biden agenda - an agenda that has taken money from our pockets and left families scrambling over the holiday season to put food on their tables and access COVID-19 tests. This strong quarter clearly demonstrates that people have grown tired of the inept leadership of Joe Biden and the pathetic excuses Democrats in Congress like Josh Gottheimer continue to make for him. Real change is coming this November." - Nick De Gregorio
In addition to raising this impressive sum as a first-time candidate since exploring a run in October 2021, De Gregorio proudly announced the endorsement of District 39 Assemblyman Robert Auth (R, Old Tappan) and Assemblywoman DeAnne DeFuccio (R, Upper Saddle River).
"Nick is our choice to represent us in Congress because we know he will use the same strength and determination as he did while honorably serving his country overseas to fight for the Fifth District in Congress," said Auth and DeFuccio.
They continued: "Washington is leaderless and broken. Politicians like Joe Biden, Nancy Pelosi, and their enabler Josh Gottheimer have only made life harder and more unaffordable for families here in New Jersey. Inflation - thanks to socialist spending sprees supported by Josh - is spiraling out of control and press releases and letters just won't cut it anymore. We need someone with a backbone to stand up and finally say no for all of us."

clean_body: Announces Endorsements of LD39 Assembly Members | | | | | | | == | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Press@NickForNJ.com January 14, 2022 De Gregorio Raises $403,000 in Challenge to Gottheimer, Announces Endorsements of LD39 Assembly Members FAIR LAWN - Today, Nick De Gregorio, a Marine Veteran and Republican Candidate for Congress in New Jersey's Fifth Congressional District, announced that his campaign will report over $403,000 raised on his year-end report for 2021 with $360,000 cash on hand. "We are grateful to all of our enthusiastic supporters for meeting the great momentum we are feeling across the Fifth District with the resources we will need to take on the disastrous Biden agenda - an agenda that has taken money from our pockets and left families scrambling over the holiday season to put food on their tables and access COVID-19 tests. This strong quarter clearly demonstrates that people have grown tired of the inept leadership of Joe Biden and the pathetic excuses Democrats in Congress like Josh Gottheimer continue to make for him. Real change is coming this November." - Nick De Gregorio In addition to raising this impressive sum as a first-time candidate since exploring a run in October 2021, De Gregorio proudly announced the endorsement of District 39 Assemblyman Robert Auth (R, Old Tappan) and Assemblywoman DeAnne DeFuccio (R, Upper Saddle River). "Nick is our choice to represent us in Congress because we know he will use the same strength and determination as he did while honorably serving his country overseas to fight for the Fifth District in Congress," said Auth and DeFuccio. They continued: "Washington is leaderless and broken. Politicians like Joe Biden, Nancy Pelosi, and their enabler Josh Gottheimer have only made life harder and more unaffordable for families here in New Jersey. Inflation - thanks to socialist spending sprees supported by Josh - is spiraling out of control and press releases and letters just won't cut it anymore. | | | With COVID surging across the nation, many schools are reconsidering the idea of returning to remote learning.

---
[Donate TODAY to make your voice heard. Keep our kids in schools.](https://kiggansforcongress.cmail20.com/t/t-l-cutkhtd-yukjlhakt-j/)

I have been a strong advocate for in person education in the Virginia General Assembly and will continue to be a voice for keeping our kids in school!
We have seen remote learning’s damaging effects on our students and their mental health over this past year:

* The average child fell 5-10 points behind students who took the same test before the pandemic.
* Students’ scores in low-income areas fell almost twice as much from pre-pandemic data points.
* Emergency room visits for suicide attempts among adolescents increased 31%, and a 51% increase in girls aged 12-17.
* Children and adolescent mental health decline has been declared a national emergency.

For the benefit of our children, we have to keep our kids in school. They need socialization and interaction with their peers for proper growth and development.
We can’t let political rhetoric and scare tactics cloud what is best for our next generation!
**_[Donate $25, $50, or $100 TODAY before our kids are forced to do more at home “learning.”](https://kiggansforcongress.cmail20.com/t/t-l-cutkhtd-yukjlhakt-t/)_**
Please join me in raising your voice about this serious matter. Our children's future and the future of our nation depends on it!

|
---
**With gratitude,**
**Jen**

name: Team Northam
subject: The most consequential Virginia Governor of the modern era
disclaimer_text: Paid for by The Way Ahead
body:
Friend,

Over the past four years, Governor Northam has become the most consequential Governor in Virginia's history with a progressive record that will positively impact Virginians' lives for generations. On this final full day of the Northam Administration, we would like to thank you for putting your trust in Governor Northam. It has been an honor to serve.

Together, we have made Virginia the country’s strongest economy, secured world-class education system for Virginia students, expanded health care for more than 600,000 Virginians, and granted broadband access to more than 390,000 homes and communities.

Read on for a snapshot of some of the many significant accomplishments Governor Northam delivered for Virginia during his time as Governor.

Building the Country’s Strongest Economy:

Under Gov. Northam, Virginia has secured $80 billion in capital investment and more than 100,000 jobs — four times more investment than any previous governor.

Historic investments in agriculture and forestry represent more than $290 million in new capital investment, nearly 1,100 new jobs, and commitments to purchase more than $539 million of Virginia-grown agriculture.

Gov. Northam opened his term by negotiating the plan to welcome Amazon’s new corporate headquarters to Virginia—a $2.5 billion investment that will result in at least 37,000 jobs.

Virginia has been named the country’s ‘Top State for Business’ three years in a row.

Virginia closed Fiscal Year 2021—the pandemic year—with a record surplus: $3.2 billion.

Gov. Northam leaves office proposing more than $3.8 billion in financial reserves. That’s 16.8% of state revenues—and more than eight times the amount Virginia had in the bank when he took office. In 2018, those same reserves stood at just $440 million, so he set a then-ambitious goal to get to 8% during his four-year term. Four years later, he’s doubled that goal. This is unprecedented in Virginia history.

Giving Virginia Kids a World-Class Education:

Since 2018 Virginia has more than doubled public Pre-K funding to serve a record total of more than 25,000 three and four year olds.

Virginia has expanded access to affordable child care to more families than ever before, serving over 27,000 children and exceeding pre-pandemic participation.

Virginia has increased teacher salaries more than 10% under Gov. Northam—the largest increase in 15 years.

Gov. Northam’s final budget proposes another 10% pay raise for teachers. This will push Virginia’s teacher pay above the national average.

Gov. Northam has made it easier to go to college:

Virginia has made the largest-ever investment in Historically Black Colleges and Universities—the total has soared 87% to more than $500 million.

Students attending Virginia high schools are now eligible for financial aid and in-state tuition, regardless of their citizenship status.

Virginia’s tuition-free community college now helps working people who choose career paths in high-demand fields.

Ensuring Healthy Living for Virginians:

More than 600,000 Virginians now have health care coverage, thanks to Gov. Northam’s successful push for Virginia to expand Medicaid.

Virginia has delivered a top-10 COVID vaccination rate among the states: 88% of Virginia adults have received at least one shot—more than 6.3 million people. 77% of Virginia adults are fully vaccinated.

Virginia is investing in mental health services—with a $315 million bond package to replace Central State Hospital.

Gov. Northam signed the Virginia Reproductive Health Protection Act into law, ending politically-motivated “TRAP” restrictions on women’s health centers and repealing Virginia’s mandatory ultrasound law and 24-hour waiting period prior to an abortion.

Investing in workers:

Gov. Northam signed legislation increasing Virginia’s minimum wage—and charting a path to a $15 minimum wage. Long overdue, this was Virginia’s first increase since 2009.

Gov. Northam secured a 5% pay increase for state employees to address ongoing recruitment and retention issues within the state workforce.

Gov. Northam championed legislation protecting employees against worker misclassification and wage theft—and banning workplace discrimination against people who are pregnant, people with disabilities, and on the basis of sexual orientation.

Gov. Northam signed the Virginia Values Act into law—becoming the first Southern state to say No to discrimination. The law makes the Commonwealth the first state in the South to enact comprehensive protections for the LGBTQ+ community against discrimination in housing, employment, public spaces, and credit applications.

Thanks to Gov. Northam’s leadership, Virginia now provides eight weeks of paid parental leave for state employees for the birth or adoption of a child.

Strengthening Civil Rights and Participation in Democracy:

Even as other states make voting harder, under Gov. Northam, Virginia is making it easier to vote.

Virginia’s 45-day early-voting period is now one of the longest in the country.

Virginia now allows voters to vote absentee—no excuses required.

Virginia now makes voter registration automatic through DMV.

Virginia has made Election Day a state holiday.

Gov. Northam is making sure people receive the second chances they deserve: The governor has restored the civil rights and voting rights of more than 112,000 individuals—and he has granted more than 700 pardons. That’s more than the last nine Governors combined.

Gov. Northam established the Commission to Examine Racial Inequity in Virginia Law to identify laws—and repeal—outdated laws that have the effect of promoting or enabling racial discrimination or inequity.

Gov. Northam proposed and signed into law elimination of the holiday honoring Confederate generals—and made state holidays of both Election Day and Juneteenth.

Gov. Northam created Virginia’s first-ever Governor’s LGBTQ+ Advisory Board. This collaboration led to new laws prohibiting discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations on the on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Gov. Northam championed ratification of the long-overdue Equal Rights amendment—making Virginia the 38th state to ratify.

Investing in Infrastructure:

Gov. Northam took aggressive steps to secure more than $2 billion to expand broadband—putting Virginia on track to achieve universal coverage by 2024, becoming one of the first states to achieve this important goal.

When the governor took office, Virginia was putting just $4 million into broadband expansion. Estimates showed Virginia had more than 660,000 unserved homes and businesses. Thanks to his work, Virginia has secured $2 billion in public-private investments to expand broadband access to more than 390,000 homes and businesses in unserved communities, especially in rural areas, small towns, and cities—and to do it four years sooner than the original goal.

Under Gov. Northam’s leadership, Virginia has delivered generational investments in infrastructure, including:

$2.2 billion to fix I-81

$3.8 billion to expand the Hampton Roads Bridge Tunnel; and

$3.7 billion to transform rail across Virginia.

Virginia negotiated an agreement with Elizabeth River Crossings to reduce tolls 50% for low-income Virginians on their daily commutes.

Gov. Northam championed and signed legislation creating dedicated funding for Metro for the first time in the system’s history.

Protecting Public Safety and Reforming Criminal Justice:

Under Gov. Northam, Virginia finally passed common-sense laws to prevent gun violence—to keep communities safer by keeping prohibited persons away from firearms. The laws:

Require background checks on all gun sales.

Enact a Substantial Risk Protective Order.

Require reporting of lost and stolen firearms.

Strengthen the law to prevent children from accessing firearms.

Reinstate Virginia’s successful one-handgun-a-month policy—first passed 30 years ago.

Prohibit firearms at polling places.

Prohibit possession of firearms by persons subject to protective orders.

Gov. Northam proposed and signed the law abolishing the death penalty in Virginia—becoming the first Southern state to end capital punishment.

Gov. Northam signed landmark legislation to legalize possession of marijuana and seal the records of prior convictions. The law creates a new Cannabis Control Authority, establishing a regulatory and licensing structure for a safe and equitable marijuana industry. The law takes effect three years earlier than originally proposed, and includes provisions to protect public health and safety, as well as the rights of people working in the new industry.

Gov. Northam led Virginia’s efforts to prevent violence and rebuild trust between law enforcement and the communities they serve. These include:

Becoming the first state in the country to ban no-knock search warrants (Breonna’s Law).

Requiring universal training on de-escalation techniques for law enforcement officers.

Limiting the circumstances under which law enforcement can use deadly force, including neck restraints (choke-holds)—and requiring officers to intervene if they witness another officer using excessive force.

Creating a statewide “Marcus Alert” system for responding to mental health crises.

Advancing Community Policing—requiring law enforcement officers to collect demographic information during all traffic and investigatory stops.

Virginia gave one-time bonuses of $3,000 to $5,000 to public safety officials in 2021, in addition to a one-time bonus of $500 in 2020. Governor Northam’s final budget proposes more than $223 million in pay increases for State Troopers, correctional officers, deputy sheriffs and regional jail officers, building on his record of law enforcement pay raises over the past four years.

Worked across the aisle to increase the ‘felony larceny threshold’ to $1,000. It had been just $200—the lowest level in the nation—since 1980.

Maintained one of the lowest rates of recidivism in the country at 23.9%, thanks to investments in re-entry programs in the Department of Corrections.

Provided bonuses of up to $5,000 for the Virginia State Police, Sheriff’s Deputies, and Jail Officers.

Ended the oppressive suspension of driver’s licenses for nonpayment of court costs, benefiting up to 600,000 Virginians.

Increased safety on Virginia roads and improved the lives of undocumented immigrants and their families by issuing more than 39,000 driver privilege cards.

Vetoed legislation to expand mandatory minimum sentencing, and pledged to veto all future legislation to expand mandatory minimums in Virginia.

Protecting the Environment:

Under the leadership of Gov. Northam, Virginia has created the strongest Chesapeake Bay cleanup plan in Virginia history. Virginia now provides more funding for the Bay than under any previous governor—$756 million to help farmers, localities, and wastewater treatment operations reduce pollution from nutrients and sediment.

Under the Virginia Clean Economy Act, Virginia now has its first renewable energy portfolio standard and energy targets to transition Virginia to 100 percent clean energy by 2050.

Gov. Northam signed legislation for Virginia to become the first southern state to join the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative. The initiative is a collaborative effort among Mid-Atlantic and Northeast states to combat climate change and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector, while driving economic growth.

Gov. Northam signed the Clean Energy and Community Flood Preparedness Act to cap climate change emissions from power plants, initiate a 30 percent reduction in the next 10 years, and generate more than $1 billion for energy efficiency and flood protection projects through the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative.

Gov. Northam led Virginia’s effort to implement science-based management of Atlantic menhaden—a small fish that’s an important part of the food web in the Chesapeake Bay.

Gov. Northam opened Machicomoco, Virginia’s 40th State Park—and the first dedicated to telling the history and stories of Virginia Indians.

Governor Northam signed historic legislation to clean up more than 27 million cubic yards of coal ash.

Virginia negotiated and passed an agreement to improve oversight of electric utility rates and enact historic mandates for investments in energy efficiency and clean power.

Gov. Northam repeatedly vetoed bills to hamstring Virginia’s fight against climate change—and established a groundbreaking new effort to strengthen resilience to sea level rise and extreme weather.

Promoting Inclusion and Transparency:

Under Gov. Northam’s leadership, Virginia now requires all state agencies and state higher-education institutions to establish and maintain a comprehensive plan for diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Virginia saw removal of statues dedicated to lost causes, thanks to partnership between Gov. Northam, the General Assembly, and the Office of AG Mark Herring. These include the statue of Robert E. Lee on Monument Avenue in Richmond (the largest Confederate monument in the country), the statue of Harry Byrd Sr. on Capitol Square, the Robert E. Lee statue at the United States Capitol, and the Arch honoring Confederate Jefferson Davis at Fort Monroe. Gov. Northam signed legislation to give localities the authority to remove monuments.

Gov. Northam established the Office of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, and appointed the country’s first Cabinet-level Chief Diversity Officer.

Gov. Northam delivered the most diverse slate of appointments to state boards and commissions in Virginia history.

Honoring Veterans:

Under Gov. Northam, Virginia doubled the number of veterans hired. The Virginia Values Veterans program set a goal to hire more than 65,000 veterans—and blew past that goal... with more than 81,000 veterans hired. That’s more than double the 31,000 veterans hired in 2018, when Gov. Northam took office.

Virginia wrote new laws prohibiting discrimination in public accommodations, employment, and housing based on a person’s military status.

Virginia passed new legislation to expand the Military Medics and Corpsmen program that helps medical personnel transition from the military to the civilian workforce.

Gov. Northam’s final budget increases tuition reimbursement for National Guard members to $1 million annually.

As the nation's only physician who is also a Governor now prepares to return to seeing children at his medical practice, we thank you, Governor Northam, for your service to Virginia.

Paid for by The Way Ahead

PO Box 597
Richmond VA 23218

body:
Fellow Patriot:

They just can't admit they were wrong.
That's the real story about Democrats and Dr. Fauci
and the panicked Covid scolds. Yes, they are drunk on power. Yes,
they love the media adulation and feeling like they are better
than everyone else.
But what it really comes down to is arrogance. After
two years, we know they were wrong:

About China.
About masks.
About vaccine mandates.
About school closures.
About natural immunity.
About everything.

But they can't admit it. They won't. And so they
continue to abuse their power, our rights, and our children.
For two years, the strongest voice in Congress
against the arrogance of the public health deep state has been
Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky.

At Senate hearings, in public forums, and on the
Senate floor, Sen. Paul has been asking the right questions and
exposing all the wrong answers.

The media says Rand gives Dr. Fauci hell, but Rand's
just giving him THE TRUTH, and he thinks it's hell!

We're supporting Rand Paul and we hope you will too.

Rand is not going to let up. Our children's future
is at stake. They have already lost two years of education due to
the teacher unions' scam of "distance learning." And even now,
with public pushback and falling test scores and science saying
children aren't at risk, they persist in their paranoia.

Here's how Sen. Paul - Dr. Paul - described it:

"It was the policy for most of modern medicine that
if kids were sick they were sent home. If a bunch of kids were
sick then we might close the school for a couple of days. But
we're not doing that. We're doing mass testing of people that are
not sick. We're sending people home that have no symptoms, and
we're testing whole classes and sending more people home... We
need to get rid of the hysteria, but the people that are
promoting the hysteria work for the government!"

He's right and conservatives need to support him for
telling the truth and not backing down!
"This is Dr. Fauci's fault," Sen. Paul said on a
recent Fox News appearance, "because he's still hysterically
talking about mandates and shutting people down and not letting
people fly and blaming the unvaccinated."

After two years, the American people know that Dr.
Fauci and the political establishment lied to us about Covid-19.
The real pandemic now is their incompetence.

Senate Conservatives Fund is proud to support Rand
Paul in his 2022 re-election campaign. He may be the conservative
movement's indispensable leader in the Covid Era.

As a doctor, a Senator, and a principled, fighting
conservative, Paul has at times almost single-handedly fought the
left-wing public health bureaucracy... and he's winning.

Please support his campaign with a generous donation
today.

SCF will pay all processing fees and transfer 100%
of your contribution to his campaign.

Joe Biden's CDC Director is now so afraid of public
debate that she is reportedly just making up Covid guidance as
she goes, with the help of media consultants, but without any
scientific input at all!

We need Rand Paul back next year along with a new
class of courageous, outspoken champions of individual liberty.

Our kids and our country deserve better than the
politicized science and fraudulent policies now coming out of
Washington.

Please join us in supporting Sen. Rand Paul and our
group of outstanding Senate candidates!

Thank you for considering this urgent request and
for doing so much to fight for America's future.

Sincerely,

Mary Vought
Executive Director
Senate Conservatives Fund

subject: God is using medical science, including vaccinations, to save us today.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Nelson for Wisconsin**
body:
---
| | "Why do we think that we can create something better than God in terms of combating disease?” – Ron Johnson

“Why do we think that God is _not_ using scientists to answer our prayers for healing and life in this pandemic?” – Rev. Steve Nelson, Tom’s dad

True story. When my son Tom Nelson (candidate for US Senate) was nine months old he was a very sick boy.

We found him in his parsonage crib on the Sunday before Christmas 1976 in obvious distress. He was feverish and stiff. As we talked and prayed and wondered what to do, it became clear to us that we had to act. We called the ambulance.

In rural Stockholm, Wisconsin, this meant calling the man who wore many hats—funeral director, furniture salesman, and on this morning, ambulance driver. In short order he and his assistant arrived, loaded our son into the coach, and took off for St. John’s Hospital in Red Wing, Minnesota, 30 miles distant.

Thomas’ doctor met us there. He examined him, noted his rapid pulse, and began to treat his heart condition. He was a sincere Christian, and each time he came in to see Tom he also offered a prayer.

Through the afternoon, however, Thomas became sicker and sicker. Finally, with the prodding of my Mom (“Steve, you have to do something!”), I requested a second opinion.

A pediatrician from the clinic came, took one look at Thomas, ordered a spinal tap, and within minutes Tom was on his way to the ICU. The lab test confirmed Dr. Schulenberg’s suspicion: spinal meningitis.

Our prayers for Thomas were answered in the person of a pediatrician experienced in childhood diseases. He used a cocktail of antibiotics to help Tom fight for his life. He was an answer to the other doctor’s prayer. Our pediatrician used faith _and_ the latest and best medical science to save our son. If we had stuck with the first doctor Tom would not be here today.

[Please support my son, Tom, in his bid to defeat Ron Johnson.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/40683688/325452715/1053214558?amount=10&refcode=TN_EM_FR_1MO_220113_1_1&refcode2=c0ffcb54-5775-ec11-94f6-c896650d4442&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84Njk2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMGZmY2I1NC01Nzc1LWVjMTEtOTRmNi1jODk2NjUwZDQ0NDIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xq_59sM1gTzLjdmPab_hDPjBGVg81S8esTgmLvFSsWo=)

This reminds me of an old story I used in my preaching days. A very devout guy is in his house when horrendous rains start falling. The water begins to rise, and before long it becomes a major flood. The roads are covered in water making driving impossible. After a while a boat comes along.

A rescue worker in the boat yells, “Come on! We’re here to save you! Get in the boat!” The guy in the house responds, “No! I’ve got faith that God will save me!”

After an unsuccessful rescue attempt, the boat leaves. The water continues to rise, and the guy is forced up to the second floor of his home.

The county sheriff’s boat comes along, and the sheriff yells, “Come on! You are going to drown if you don’t get in the boat.” From his second floor window the guy says, “No! I’ll be okay! I have faith God will save me.” The boat moves on.

The house, except for a small part on the roof, is submerged in water. The guy is on the roof as a helicopter hovers overhead. The pilot shouts out, “This is your last chance! Climb up the ladder to safety! If you don’t come now you’re going to drown!”

The guy hollers, “No, thanks! God is going to save me!” The pilot shrugs his shoulders and flies away.

The house is covered, and the guy is swept away by the flood waters. He ascends to the Pearly Gates, where God is waiting for his arrival.

We found him in his parsonage crib on the Sunday before Christmas 1976 in obvious distress. He was feverish and stiff. As we talked and prayed and wondered what to do, it became clear to us that we had to act. We called the ambulance. In rural Stockholm, Wisconsin, this meant calling the man who wore many hats—funeral director, furniture salesman, and on this morning, ambulance driver. In short order he and his assistant arrived, loaded our son into the coach, and took off for St. John’s Hospital in Red Wing, Minnesota, 30 miles distant. Thomas’ doctor met us there. He examined him, noted his rapid pulse, and began to treat his heart condition. He was a sincere Christian, and each time he came in to see Tom he also offered a prayer. Through the afternoon, however, Thomas became sicker and sicker. Finally, with the prodding of my Mom (“Steve, you have to do something!”), I requested a second opinion. A pediatrician from the clinic came, took one look at Thomas, ordered a spinal tap, and within minutes Tom was on his way to the ICU. The lab test confirmed Dr. Schulenberg’s suspicion: spinal meningitis. Our prayers for Thomas were answered in the person of a pediatrician experienced in childhood diseases. body:
# [#]Team,

As we begin such an important year for our campaign, I have big news.

After waiting on the edge of our seats for months, the NJ Congressional Redistricting Commission has finally voted to approve a brand new congressional district map – and with a new map comes new voters.

This new map sees New Jersey’s 5th congressional district lose its towns from Warren County and gain eight towns from Bergen County, including Englewood, Englewood Cliffs, Cresskill, Fort Lee, Leonia, Palisades Park, Ridgefield Park and Tenafly. Eight towns – that’s a lot of new voters.

On top of all of that, Governor Murphy won my new district by only one point in 2021!!

But this isn’t my first time running in an intense, high-stakes election. In order to win in the new 5th congressional district, I will need to connect with thousands of new voters. I need to show them that I care about their families, their towns, and the issues that affect them every single day. I'll also be on the lookout for issues that have long gone unsolved so I can bring something new to the table for these people. First impressions are everything when it comes to new voters, and I want to make lasting ones.

So, with the new year, new voters, and new opponents, it’s officially crunch time. But, I can’t do all of this without your help. Campaigning in a new district is going to require time, effort, and money.

Your contribution will help us be as prepared as possible to take on the new year (and everything it may bring with it) in stride. Will you consider chipping in to ensure I can continue to represent you for another congressional term? statewide.
This is already shaping up to be one of the most expensive gubernatorial primaries in Maryland’s history, with millions of dollars pouring into Maryland from out-of-state millionaires and special interest groups during this election. Ours has been a campaign focused on earning the trust, support, and votes of Marylanders – the residents, families, and business owners who make our communities strong – and we will continue to do so in the coming weeks and months leading up to the June 28th primary.
Thanks to you, we have met and exceeded our fundraising goal and we have the resources we need to fuel this campaign to victory.
To those that contributed to our campaign to meet our target, thank you.
Because of supporters like you, our momentum is growing, and we remain closer to the finish line than any other candidate in the race. It is critical, now more than ever, that Maryland elects a Governor and a Lt. Governor with the vision, the experience, and the leadership needed to lift our communities into the high quality of life that they deserve. Together, we’ll work with leaders and communities across the state to deliver results, not rhetoric, to make Maryland a more equitable and prosperous state.

This Saturday, Donald Trump is coming back to Arizona. He knows how important this state is, and he knows how important our race is. | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/40685823/325462632/1927938479?refcode=20220114_MK_split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMGNhNTlmNy01Yjc1LWVjMTEtOTRmNi1jODk2NjUwZDQ0NDIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tUbxCKbvp27rO_k5KyaFBxEWuWOS-lExXEZwufSiCOk=)
Friends — Tomorrow, Donald Trump is coming back to Arizona. He knows how important this state is, and he knows how important our race is. That’s why last time he was here, he said “Taking America back begins with kicking Mark Kelly the hell out of the United States Senate.” And the truth is, if we don’t have the resources we need to win this race, he might get his wish. If he can help flip this seat in 2022, it might make him more likely to run (and win) in 2024. Sorry to put that thought in your head, but it’s true. That’s why we’re asking if you can make a contribution before Trump arrives. name: Christina Davidson
subject: It’s none of my business…
body:
I don't know you and you don't know me, but the government is forcing me to choose between the jab and my job, and I'm writing to you today because I think we have something important in common. I think you're a patriot, and I think you know what's at stake. You know that freedoms given away are never given back... [](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/BC.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c210334%7c8339%7c8%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz%7c805&wdmdk=%2fiAkBOLEcedb8tcebQnpjQ&sysid=1)
I don't know you and you don't know me, but the government is forcing me to choose between the jab and my job, and I'm writing to you today because I think we have something important in common. I think you're a patriot, and I think you know what's at stake. You know that freedoms given away are never given back... |
I don't know you and you don't know me, but the government is forcing me to choose between the jab and my job, and I'm writing to you today because I think we have something important in common.

I think you're a patriot, and I think you know what's at stake.

You know that freedoms given away are never given back.

And no matter your vaccination status, you know that your medical decisions are between you and your doctor - not you and your government, or you and your boss.

**That's why I'm suing the federal government alongside of 6,000 other federal employees with the help of the Health Freedom Defense Fund and why I hope I can count on your generous support today.**

[**Will you give $25, $50, $100 or more and give us the ammunition we need to win this legal battle?**](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c12580%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=NS2gKQ1Ufe9ndHq9f10VMQ&sysid=1)

My name is Christina Davidson, I'm a paramedic firefighter, and I've worked for the Department of Defense for 14 years.

**_If I did what the government is doing I'd lose my license on the spot._**

I'm not allowed to give my patients medication without their consent, and I'm not allowed to threaten them to take medication.

But that's exactly what's happening to me and thousands of other employees across the country, and that's why we need you on our side.

_Because what starts with us won't end with us._

**If they can do it to me, they can do it to you.**

We're taking on this legal battle because we know if we give up and give in, it's only a matter of time before they come after you, your livelihood and your family the way they came after ours.

We want to stop tyranny in its tracks and codify our medical rights into law once and for all.

[**But we don't stand a chance without you.**](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c12581%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=CGrldPwcDjrm2eVAaMDwsA&sysid=1)

I won't mince words...we've got our work cut out for us.

The government is going to fight us every step of the way.

They've already shown us how far they're willing to go to push these mandates.

They've blatantly defied the courts, and are encouraging private employers to do the same. The President has even told businesses to ignore the courts.

Federal employees lucky enough to get an exemption are required to undergo "reeducation" training.

On top of regular threats, we're told we have no chance of promotion unless we shut up and take it.

And if we're fired, it won't just be a matter of finding a new job.

They're making it so that we'll never be able to find work again.

They want to make us so desperate that we have no choice but to surrender once and for all.

This has nothing to do with health.

**They want to break our wills, break our spirits, and send a loud, clear message that they have control over our lives.**

And if we let them win, there's no turning back.

[**Which is why I hope you'll fight along with me with a generous gift of $25 or more today to help fund lawsuits to fight vaccine mandates and preserve medical freedom.**](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c12582%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=hYIsM3L7WbDF%2bpSPwhz9bQ&sysid=1)

**I don't know if you're vaccinated - and I don't want to know.**

It's none of my business.

I want to know if you'll stand up for your countrymen when it matters most.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Christina Davidson
Paramedic & Firefighter
For the Health Freedom Defense Fund

| | Hi Friends,

This weekend please help find supporters at the American Digger's Gun Show, doors open at 9:00 a.m. in the Omar Shrine Temple, 176 Patriots Point Rd, Mt Pleasant.

Please, be respectful at the event because the events Host would not allow me to have a table inside. They told me we could place materials on an information table. They also said I can have supporters attend and speak to whomever we want. Please, bring your cameras and take pictures of the people. Take great group pictures of everyone with their HATS on having fun!

Find Kyle Hulse to get a campaign cap, palm cards, supporter sign-up sheets, etc. You can spot him wearing a cap or call him at 716-713-5455. Please email him at ubbull90@yahoo.com to tell him you'll be there. I'd be glad to pay you back for your $10 admission, just let me know you went to the show.

Omar Shrine Temple, 176 Patriots Point Rd, Mt Pleasant**
**1/17/22 Martin Luther King Day events TBD**
**1/29/22 from 12:00 – 3:00 p.m. John McCant Park FundRaiser, Goose Creek. **Bill Graves who lives in Goose Creek has planned many events and is retired Navy. Bill works at the American Legion in Goose Creek and is leading this outdoor event. Please contact him at [williamgraves27@yahoo.com](mailto:williamgraves27@yahoo.com) and Linda Ensor at [centurionscheduler@gmail.com](mailto:centurionscheduler@gmail.com) if you can help at the event.
**2/19/22 from 6:00 - 8:00 p.m Summerville VFW Post 3433, Fundraiser, Invites list. **

I want volunteers to shoot photos of me meeting voters, pass out my literature, take names of supporters and new volunteers, or speak in my place if I can't attend and meet the community. Are you are member of a group or organization you could garner support with for me as my spokesperson?****

| | here is what is happening in the fight to secure our elections, protect the right to vote, and defend our democracy: Yesterday, the House voted on a bill that combines the Freedom to Vote Act and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. We sent it over to the Senate using a legislative maneuver (I will not bore you with the details) that ensures that the Senate will actually be forced to debate it, rather than allowing obstructionists to filibuster even _starting_ the debate. Of course, the filibuster can still be used to block the vote. I am hopeful that when push comes to shove, the Senate will change its rules and finally allow a basic majority-rules up-or-down vote on this crucial legislation. In addition to ending partisan gerrymandering, disclosing dark money, expanding opportunities to vote, and restoring voting rights protections, this bill will ensure that our votes are counted accurately. As President Biden said, "It's about election subversion, not just whether or not people get to vote. Who counts the vote? That's what this is about, that's what makes this so different from anything else we've ever done." We have to get this done. And if it does not get done this weekend, I am going to keep up the fight to get it done "as long as I have a breath in me", as President Biden said.

Of course, the filibuster can still be used to block the vote. I am hopeful that when push comes to shove, the Senate will change its rules and finally allow a basic majority-rules up-or-down vote on this crucial legislation. In addition to ending partisan gerrymandering, disclosing dark money, expanding opportunities to vote, and restoring voting rights protections, this bill will ensure that our votes are counted accurately. As President Biden said, "It's about election subversion, not just whether or not people get to vote. Who counts the vote? That's what this is about, that's what makes this so different from anything else we've ever done." We have to get this done. And if it does not get done this weekend, I am going to keep up the fight to get it done "as long as I have a breath in me", as President Biden said. | **_On the State of the State, Congress of Counties_**
---
|
---
_File Photo: Chairman Kyle Hupfer speaks at the 2020 Congress of Counties._
| I was honored to attend Governor Holcomb's sixth State of the State Address in-person this past Tuesday. As we've come to expect, he delivered his address full of passion and with an unmatched enthusiasm about our state's future. And while there were many great moments throughout, my personal favorite was when he reminded our law enforcement that we have their back, stating, "To Indiana’s law enforcement community, I say, we say, 'Thank you' and 'We’ve got your back!'" The chamber erupted in applause and gave our law enforcement a much-deserved standing ovation.

I also wanted to remind you of the upcoming Congress of Counties event in French Lick, Ind., on February 25-26. This two-day training and networking conference is for Republican Party leaders, candidates, grassroots activists, volunteers, and anyone who is interested in moving our state forward. Senator Todd Young will be joining us as a special guest for our Friday reception...you won't want to miss it! You can find more information about the event **[here](https://indgop.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=89fb3de929a99eecb88e6fb27&id=3cdf809029&e=1acd9bb3d6)**.

Enjoy this week's newsletter and share it with a friend.

Best,

Chairman Kyle Hupfer

| **_Strong Like Indiana Steel_**
---
|
---
_Gov. Holcomb delivers his 2022 State of the State Address._
|
---
_Gov. Holcomb smiles and looks to the gallery after recognizing a special guest at the 2022 State of the State Address._
| This past Tuesday, Governor Holcomb delivered his 2022 State of the State Address, his sixth since taking office. In it, he presented a bold plan to further Indiana’s historic momentum and lead us out of the pandemic.

It's worth watching and reading in its entirety, which you can do **[here](https://indgop.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=89fb3de929a99eecb88e6fb27&id=8f7e57a833&e=1acd9bb3d6)** and **[here](https://indgop.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=89fb3de929a99eecb88e6fb27&id=4f41a8fe07&e=1acd9bb3d6)** , but we've provided some quick highlights below:

__Economy__ _:_ Years of strong Republican leadership have put the state in an unprecedented financial position, and the stats back it up.

__Education and Workforce Development__ _:_ A historic investment in new education dollars combined with a deeper alignment of our educational, talent, and career pathways will ensure that the Indiana economy continues to boom, and Hoosiers thrive.

__Health and Wellness:__ Indiana has made progress in areas like reducing infant mortality, but there is more work to be done to truly be firing on all cylinders.

__Community Development:__ Indiana is maintaining its aggressive pace to build a 21st-century infrastructure network that links Hoosiers to each other, the nation, and a world of opportunities.

__Good Government Service:____ Gov. Holcomb will continue to partner with local communities on public safety efforts and deliver good government service.

You can check out our Twitter thread **[here](https://indgop.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=89fb3de929a99eecb88e6fb27&id=1fc29f3a9f&e=1acd9bb3d6) **of some of the most memorable quotes of the night.

| **_Sullivan Officially Files for 2022 Convention_**
---
| [ ](https://indgop.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=89fb3de929a99eecb88e6fb27&id=1f2fd952aa&e=1acd9bb3d6)
---
_Sullivan announces her filing._
| This past Monday, our Secretary of State, Holli Sullivan, officially filed to be a candidate at the 2022 Indiana Republican State Convention.

“As Secretary of State I know how much is at stake. I’m running because safe and secure elections is not a destination. It is a relentless pursuit to ensure that all eligible voters are able to cast a ballot and all legal votes are counted in a timely manner, free of fraud, corruption and interference, stated Sullivan.

"Here in Indiana, we have safe and secure elections with our strong voter ID laws and our transparent process for maintaining current and accurate voter rolls. Democrats and their allies are trying to federalize our elections. We can never let this happen. Hoosier elections should always be run by Hoosiers."

You can watch her announcement video **above**.

name: Karen Bass
subject: Memo: Plan for Los Angeles to fight homelessness and end street encampments.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Karen Bass for Mayor 2022 (ID # 1441328)
body:
Hello,

As you read this, more than 40,000 Angelenos are experiencing homelessness. And over 350,000 Angelenos are at risk of becoming homeless.

Our city's homelessness crisis is reaching a boiling point. It's a crisis for the unhoused and for our neighborhoods. It's a crisis on every level – public health, public safety, economic, and humanitarian – and it requires a bold and aggressive emergency response.

**That’s why today, I’m announcing my plan to house 15,000 individuals by the end of year one, dramatically reduce street homelessness, end street encampments, and lead on mental health and substance abuse treatment.**

For too many years, government action on homelessness has been siloed. Federal, state, county, and city governments have all moved in different directions — with no coordination or overarching plan. That simply can't happen any longer; there is no time to waste. I'm the only candidate for Mayor with the experience and qualifications to bring everyone to the table, including federal, state, county, and city governments, and implement a single plan that cuts through the bureaucracy, actually addresses mental health and substance abuse issues, and brings home every available dollar to solve homelessness.

This should be the #1 priority of anyone who is serious about running for Mayor of Los Angeles, and it's certainly mine. That's why I'm releasing my very first policy plan on how to tackle homelessness in Los Angeles.
1. As Mayor, I will lead on homelessness and personally drive action at City Hall to fight homelessness and end all street encampments. And I’ll appoint and empower one individual – who reports directly to the Mayor – to carry out this vision. Personality conflicts and bureaucratic turf battles will not be tolerated. And every dollar budgeted for homelessness will actually go to solve homelessness – no accounting tricks, no added bureaucracy.

2. Temporary housing is not the solution to homelessness but it is critically needed to help get people off the streets as soon as possible, and provide a bridge to permanent housing. We must also be relentless when it comes to building more affordable and permanent supportive housing if we want to solve this crisis. That’s why as Mayor, I will work with the community and take urgent action to get as much temporary and permanent housing up and running as quickly as possible.

3. As part of my coordinated emergency response to homelessness, we will deploy trained neighborhood service teams across Los Angeles – because the only way to successfully transition individuals from the streets to housing and services is through persistent on-the-ground engagement and outreach. Our strategic approach, which will lead to the vast majority of individuals accepting offers of housing, and then triage the small number of individuals that don't, will lead to the end of encampments.

4. Nearly fifty percent of unsheltered individuals are either suffering from severe mental illness or substance abuse. My Administration will lead on mental health and substance abuse treatment. I stand ready to take the lead in working with the county, state, and federal governments to address the severe shortage of mental health and substance use disorder services, support, and capacity.

5. Individuals become homeless for different reasons and we should target job training and employment assistance accordingly. As Mayor, I will promote access to social support services to make sure that individuals can access safety net programs. And I'll locate robust job training and counseling services in both temporary and permanent housing that can help get people back into the workforce.

The best way to prevent homelessness is to keep folks in their homes. I will make housing vouchers work for more Angelenos and maximize resources for rental assistance, direct cash assistance, and low-interest loan programs to ensure that we keep our neighbors safely housed, even when money is tight.

There is no one-size-fits-all solution to our homelessness crisis. Those experiencing homelessness are from all walks of life, and a disproportionate number are Black, Latino, LGBTQ+, and/or formerly incarcerated people. I will pay special attention to the unique populations who find themselves homeless for very different reasons – and be relentless in addressing the root causes of homelessness to prevent folks from becoming homeless in the first place.

If you're ready to help end this humanitarian crisis, here's how I could use your help:

clean_body: Hello, As you read this, more than 40,000 Angelenos are experiencing homelessness. And over 350,000 Angelenos are at risk of becoming homeless. Our city's homelessness crisis is reaching a boiling point. It's a crisis for the unhoused and for our neighborhoods. It's a crisis on every level – public health, public safety, economic, and humanitarian – and it requires a bold and aggressive emergency response. That’s why today, I’m announcing my plan to house 15,000 individuals by the end of year one, dramatically reduce street homelessness, end street encampments, and lead on mental health and substance abuse treatment. For too many years, government action on homelessness has been siloed. Federal, state, county, and city governments have all moved in different directions — with no coordination or overarching plan. That simply can't happen any longer; there is no time to waste. I'm the only candidate for Mayor with the experience and qualifications to bring everyone to the table, including federal, state, county, and city governments, and implement a single plan that cuts through the bureaucracy, actually addresses mental health and substance abuse issues, and brings home every available dollar to solve homelessness. This should be the #1 priority of anyone who is serious about running for Mayor of Los Angeles, and it's certainly mine. That's why I'm releasing my very first policy plan on how to tackle homelessness in Los Angeles. 1. As Mayor, I will lead on homelessness and personally drive action at City Hall to fight homelessness and end all street encampments. And I’ll appoint and empower one individual – who reports directly to the Mayor – to carry out this vision. Personality conflicts and bureaucratic turf battles will not be tolerated. And every dollar budgeted for homelessness will actually go to solve homelessness – no accounting tricks, no added bureaucracy. 2. Temporary housing is not the solution to homelessness but it is critically needed to help get people off the streets as soon as possible, and provide a bridge to permanent housing. We must also be relentless when it comes to building more affordable and permanent supportive housing if we want to solve this crisis. That’s why as Mayor, I will work with the community and take urgent action to get as much temporary and permanent housing up and running as quickly as possible. 3. As part of my coordinated emergency response to homelessness, we will deploy trained neighborhood service teams across Los Angeles – because the only way to successfully transition individuals from the streets to housing and services is through persistent on-the-ground engagement and outreach. Our strategic approach, which will lead to the vast majority of individuals accepting offers of housing, and then triage the small number of individuals that don't, will lead to the end of encampments. 4. Nearly fifty percent of unsheltered individuals are either suffering from severe mental illness or substance abuse. My Administration will lead on mental health and substance abuse treatment. I stand ready to take the lead in working with the county, state, and federal governments to address the severe shortage of mental health and substance use disorder services, support, and capacity. 5. Individuals become homeless for different reasons and we should target job training and employment assistance accordingly. As Mayor, I will promote access to social support services to make sure that individuals can access safety net programs. And I'll locate robust job training and counseling services in both temporary and permanent housing that can help get people back into the workforce. The best way to prevent homelessness is to keep folks in their homes. I will make housing vouchers work for more Angelenos and maximize resources for rental assistance, direct cash assistance, and low-interest loan programs to ensure that we keep our neighbors safely housed, even when money is tight. There is no one-size-fits-all solution to our homelessness crisis. Those experiencing homelessness are from all walks of life, and a disproportionate number are Black, Latino, LGBTQ+, and/or formerly incarcerated people. I will pay special attention to the unique populations who find themselves homeless for very different reasons – and be relentless in addressing the root causes of homelessness to prevent folks from becoming homeless in the first place. If you're ready to help end this humanitarian crisis, here's how I could use your help: In solidarity, Karen P.S. Karen is building a grassroots campaign by and for the people of L.A. # ICYMI: Highlights from the Second GOP Gubernatorial Debate
**West Chester, Pa.** **\-- ** Bill McSwain, Republican candidate for Governor, on Wednesday participated in the second GOP Gubernatorial Debate at the Scottish Rite Cathedral in New Castle, hosted by the Lawrence County Republican Committee.

Throughout the course of the debate, McSwain outlined his plans to restore PA's economy, promote public safety and security, harness the Commonwealth's energy resources, and his support of the Second Amendment and constitutional carry.

In his opening remarks, McSwain promised to do whatever it takes to restore safety, security, and liberty across the Commonwealth:
---
| [ ](https://freedompapac.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b9af0aef3fa3167622552aedb&id=208ed01693&e=b1ec95759b)
---
|
---
| McSwain also shared his dedication to promoting pro-life voices and policies, as well as his plan to empower parents and implement school choice:
---
| **_"A quality education for all Pennsylvania children starts with meaningful school choice, and _**_**I am the only candidate who has issued a Parents' Bill of Rights. I support public education, but as Governor I will put students, families, and teachers first and the union bosses last - that's why I've pledged**_ _** to never take a dime from any teachers union. Every child deserves a quality education that meets their individual needs, and as Governor, I'll do whatever it takes to make sure they get it." **_
---
|
---
| McSwain also condemned the passage of Act 77 and no-excuse mail-in ballots, promising to promote election security and transparency by returning to a system of in-person voting:
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| **BACKGROUND: **

Appointed by President Trump, McSwain's record as US Attorney demonstrates his fierce defense of constitutional rights, dedication to upholding law and order, and history of putting criminals and corrupt politicians in jail. Prior to becoming an attorney, Bill served as a scout/sniper platoon commander in the U.S. Marine Corps. He was born in Philadelphia and raised in Chester County, where he lives today with his wife, Stephanie, and their four children. More information on McSwain's background and platform is available [here.](https://freedompapac.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b9af0aef3fa3167622552aedb&id=5d1aed1e12&e=b1ec95759b)

Last year, Republicans introduced a record-breaking number of voter restrictions in state legislatures.

Hey y’all. It’s Ali — Mike’s campaign manager here. In just a moment I’m going to ask if you’ll chip in to support Mike’s campaign for Lieutenant Governor of Texas. First, though, I hope you’ll give me a chance to explain why your support matters, especially right now. We’ve had such a great response since we officially launched this movement to defeat the worst Lieutenant Governor in the country, and I can’t thank you enough for that! I’m so grateful that you are as excited about what we can accomplish this year as I am. **As we begin to kick this campaign into high gear, we have been asked a common question — what are we doing differently from our 2018 campaign to make sure we finally defeat Dan Patrick?** Well, it’s my job to figure out how we’ll win, and so I wanted to report on our plan to make it happen. Since we launched, we’ve traveled more than 8,000 miles across Texas. We’ve talked to voters about solving problems and addressing the issues folks like you care about most — such as fixing the damn grid, investing in our public schools and hospitals, expanding broadband access, protecting our constitutional rights, and so much more. We’ve also asked folks for input on how we can do better as a campaign. And while the answers varied greatly, there were some clear themes in the responses. **Texans want us to focus on three things:** 1\. Investing in robust voter outreach, especially in traditionally Republican counties and in South Texas 2\. Articulating clear policy platforms on fixing the damn grid, public education, and property taxes 3\. Multiplying voter contact through a statewide field and canvassing program that includes expert volunteer training With these insights, we know where we’re going to be focusing our resources in the coming months. Reaching new voters is going to be our top priority, and it will ultimately be the way we defeat Dan Patrick. We’ll do that through a grassroots, targeted statewide program. And Mike and our team are going to keep traveling around the state, listening to Texans, and fighting to earn every vote, in every community, in every county. We won’t be able to do any of that without your support, though. It’s going to take a massive grassroots effort to fund the kind of campaign that our supporters want us to run (and that we want to run, too!). name: Justin Francese
subject: wishing Doyle a happy birthday
body:
she was in her first year at a near by college. When we met, she was holding a banner | Friend, It was Earth Day 1999. I was a senior at the University of Vermont and she was in her first year at a near by college. When we met, she was holding a banner demanding that the University cut ties with the pesticide giant, Monsanto. I knew that I had to join her. But how could I have known that my life would change forever? Since that day, we've been through 15 birthdays, a decade of marriage, putting down roots in Eugene, law school, grad school, the births of our daughter and our son, and so much more. Through it all, her passion, clear sense of purpose, and power shines through as she has taken on the righteous fights. When Doyle told me late last year that she was called to consider another run for Congress, I knew that the feedback from supporters like you would make all the difference in her decision.
